transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Jordan Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (PraxisCore CISO), Leila Chen (PraxisCore Sr. Infra), Ravi Patel (Head of ML), Sofia Moreno (Security Ops)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- High-level intake on security posture, SOC2/ISO needs, SSO/SAML and RBAC expectations, KMS/HSM preferences, audit log retention, and hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs.
- Customer leaning toward a private or dedicated path because of data residency and audit requirements; evaluating costs and key management options.
- Next steps: share SOC2/ISO artifacts, schedule private deployment technical deep-dive, send pricing worksheet.

Topics covered:
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II, ISO27001, PCI/HIPAA considerations
- Identity: SSO, SAML, OIDC, SCIM, RBAC models
- Cryptography: Customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed KMS, HSM options
- Observability & Logs: audit logs, token-level tracing, retention windows (30/90/365 days)
- Deployment: Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem
- Performance & cost tradeoffs (batching, quantization, KV cache)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Miller: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Tom Alvarez: Tom here, CISO, PraxisCore.
[00:07] Leila Chen: Leila, infra.
[00:09] Ravi Patel: Ravi, ML.
[00:11] Sofia Moreno: Sofia, sec ops.
[00:13] Priya Shah: Priya from Redwood, I'll do the technical bits.

[00:20] Jordan Miller: Great. We put together an intake — the goal today is to understand your security and compliance constraints and what you'd need to run inference with Redwood. We're expecting questions across SOC2, ISO, SSO, RBAC, KMS, audit logs, retention, and whether hosted/dedicated/private fits.

[00:35] Tom Alvarez: Yeah, big one for us is auditability and key control. We're a regulated fintech, need traceable logs, and prefer customer-managed keys if possible. SOC2 evidence is table stakes. Also ISO is a nice-to-have.

[00:48] Priya Shah: Understood. We do provide SOC2 Type II reports; happy to share our attestation. For ISO 27001, we can share the summary and controls mapping. On keys, we support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed keys — KMIP/HSM integrations are possible in private deployments, and we have KMS integrations in dedicated as well.

[01:12] Leila Chen: When you say KMS in dedicated, is that a bring-your-own-key model or just encryption at rest? We need full key separation for some datasets.

[01:22] Priya Shah: Good callout. In Dedicated you can use a customer-managed KMS in your cloud project and we can integrate via our keywrap flow. For Private (VPC/on-prem) you get full control — keys never leave your environment if you choose HSM-backed keys. For hosted API we have envelope encryption but keys are Redwood-managed by default. We can do BYOK for hosted in some enterprise arrangements but it changes the deployment model and SLAs.

[01:54] Ravi Patel: What's the impact on latency if we go BYOK/HSM? Our models need sub-200ms for smaller prompts.

[02:02] Priya Shah: Typically key operations are infrequent — auth and occasional envelope ops — so crypto itself doesn't meaningfully change per-token latency. The bigger differences come from hosting mode: hosted runs on our shared clusters, dedicated gives you reserved capacity and lower variance, and private gives network/infra control. For sub-200ms you'll want dedicated with tuned instances or private with co-located infra. There's also batching/quantization tradeoffs.

[02:35] Tom Alvarez: Audit logs — we need immutable logs for 12 months and the ability to export them to our SIEM. Is there a streaming or push capability?

[02:44] Jordan Miller: Yes, we support log export to customer destinations (S3, GCS, direct syslog ingest) and a push to SIEM. Logs include request metadata, model version, route, token counts, and anonymized or full payloads depending on configuration. There's a toggle for PII redaction; by default for hosted some payloads are redacted, but with dedicated/private you can retain full payloads in your control.

[03:15] Sofia Moreno: Quick question — how granular is RBAC? We need least privilege by team and want to restrict who can call production models versus test endpoints.

[03:23] Priya Shah: We have role-based controls that map to SSO groups via SCIM. You can create roles like model_invoke, model_manage, billing_admin, and map them to SAML/Okta groups. Audit trails tie actions back to tokens and user IDs. Some of the older APIs had coarser control, but our current console exposes per-route keys and token scoping.

[03:53] Leila Chen: Is the SCIM integration one-way or two-way? We prefer group sync from Okta.

[03:58] Priya Shah: Okta group push is supported; it's sync from your IdP into Redwood. You can also disable user provisioning if you want to manage accounts manually.

[04:10] Ravi Patel: On data residency — we will need EU-only processing for some customers. What options do we have?

[04:16] Jordan Miller: We have region routing policies. Hosted can pin to EU regions for data-in-region, but you need the proper contractual addendum. Dedicated can be provisioned in a specific region and Private gives you the most control by deploying into your VPC or on-prem.

[04:34] Tom Alvarez: Any certifications for hosting in EU data centers?

[04:38] Priya Shah: We have SOC2 Type II across our platform and some regional attestations for partners. For market-ready EU-specific certifications, we often pair Private deployments with local compliance attestations. We'll share the compliance pack after the call.

[04:54] Sofia Moreno: About retention — we want the ability to set different retention windows by dataset: e.g., ephemeral (7 days), operational (90 days), regulated (365+). Can Redwood do per-route or per-model retention policies?

[05:06] Jordan Miller: Yes, retention policies can be configured per-route. For hosted we offer defaults (30/90/365), but for dedicated and private you can set arbitrary retention rules and export/archive to your long-term storage. Audit logging retention is decoupled from payload retention.

[05:23] Leila Chen: How about access to raw request payloads for troubleshooting? We sometimes need the exact prompt.

[05:28] Priya Shah: In Dedicated/Private you can choose to retain raw payloads; in hosted they are redacted by default unless you opt in with a data processing addendum and higher tier. We'll document the toggles and controls.

[05:43] Ravi Patel: One of our ML constraints is deterministic model versions for reproducibility. Can we pin a model snapshot and ensure rollouts are controlled?

[05:51] Jordan Miller: Absolutely — our deployment layer supports version pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback policies to a compatible model variant. We'll show an example in the tech deep-dive.

[06:05] Tom Alvarez: Okay, a few practical items — incident response and breach notifications: what's your SLA for notifying customers?

[06:13] Priya Shah: We have an incident response playbook; for security incidents that affect customer data we commit to 72-hour initial notification and ongoing updates. For Dedicated/Private customers we can include tighter SLA language in enterprise contracts.

[06:28] Sofia Moreno: Do you provide proof of penetration tests or vulnerability scanning reports?

[06:33] Jordan Miller: Yes, we can share summaries of our pen tests and a redacted vulnerability management report. Full reports are usually reviewed under an NDA.

[06:44] Leila Chen: Are logs tamper-evident? We need chain-of-custody for audit.

[06:49] Priya Shah: We provide immutable log storage options when exporting to your S3/GCS with object lock for legal hold. For hosted exports we produce signed log manifests. Private gives the most control for chain of custody.

[07:10] Ravi Patel: Let's talk about telemetry. Do you provide token-level cost breakdowns? We want to reconcile charges with usage per route.

[07:18] Jordan Miller: Yes, Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, route-level dashboards, and per-token accounting. For Dedicated we can provide more granular billing exports.

[07:36] Tom Alvarez: On SSO: we use Okta and need SAML + SCIM. Any gotchas?

[07:41] Priya Shah: Okta SAML + SCIM is a common pattern. Make sure your group IDs and attribute mappings are set; we'll provide a configuration guide. We also support OIDC-based SSO for some IdPs.

[07:54] Leila Chen: We're also concerned about who can create long-lived API keys. Do you have restrictions?

[07:59] Priya Shah: Key creation can be restricted to certain roles; long-lived keys can be disabled and replaced with scoped route keys. We recommend short-lived tokens and service accounts for automation.

[08:12] Sofia Moreno: Any support for hardware-backed keys (HSM) for private deployments?

[08:16] Priya Shah: Yes, in Private we can integrate with your HSM; you can configure key access controls such that private keys never leave the HSM boundary. For Dedicated we do key wrapping using customer KMS.

[08:29] Ravi Patel: How are backups and model artifacts handled? We need to ensure model artifacts are versioned and access-controlled.

[08:35] Priya Shah: Models are treated as artifacts with versioning. Access is controlled via RBAC and audit logs. Backups for Private can be controlled by you; for Hosted we store model artifacts in our internal storage with access controls.

[08:50] Tom Alvarez: Any questions on our side?

[08:55] Leila Chen: Two clarifications — 1) For the BYOK flow, who rotates keys and how is revocation handled? 2) For audit exports, are the timestamps in UTC and do they include request IDs?

[09:04] Priya Shah: For BYOK you typically rotate keys in your KMS. If a key is revoked we support immediate rekeying and a key-wrap fallback. For logs, yes timestamps are UTC and include request IDs, model version, route, and token counts.

[09:25] Jordan Miller: I'll capture the actions — we'll send SOC2 and ISO artifacts, plus a dedicated pricing worksheet. Priya will set up a 60-minute deep dive to walk through Private deployment and KMS/HSM integration. Leila and Ravi, you'll send the retention/regulatory details and performance targets.

[09:40] Tom Alvarez: Sounds good. One more thing — what's the typical timeline for spinning up Dedicated vs Private?

[09:47] Priya Shah: Dedicated typically takes 2–4 weeks to provision once contract/signature is complete. Private depends on complexity; a simple VPC deployment can be done in 2–6 weeks, on-prem with HSM and air-gap can take longer, 6–12 weeks. We have a deployment checklist we'll share.

[10:05] Ravi Patel: Pricing sensitivity — if we go dedicated reserved capacity, can you provide example unit economics? We want to compare to self-hosting costs.

[10:14] Jordan Miller: We'll share a pricing worksheet with reserved commit levels, burst costs, and example per-token unit costs. Also we'll include a rough estimate for quantization and batching savings.

[10:26] Sofia Moreno: Security questionnaire — do you accept completed vendor security questionnaires?

[10:30] Jordan Miller: Yes, we accept them; please send and we'll return answers. For some sensitive questionnaires we request an NDA.

[10:38] Leila Chen: Can we also get a sample contract section on data processing and breach notification?

[10:43] Jordan Miller: Absolutely, I'll include a redlined sample from our standard enterprise addendum.

[10:50] Tom Alvarez: Great. If we decide to pilot, what's the simplest path? Hosted with locked retention? Or Dedicated trial?

[10:57] Priya Shah: The fastest is hosted with a data processing addendum and adjusted retention — you can get started in days. For a pilot that's meant to validate latency and throughput for production, Dedicated trial or short-term reserved capacity is recommended. Private pilot is heavier but shows full compliance posture.

[11:18] Jordan Miller: Ok last check — any blockers on our side to share docs?
[11:22] Tom Alvarez: None, please send SOC2 and the ISO summary. We'll also send you our list of regions and data categories.

[11:28] Jordan Miller: Thanks all. We'll recap and send the artifacts.

[11:33] Priya Shah: I'll follow up on scheduling the tech deep-dive and include an agenda (KMS flow, SCIM/SAML config, log export demo, deployment checklist).

[11:42] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: audio had a bit of overlap during intro; some product names transcribed as "Redwood Reserved" occasionally where speaker meant Dedicated. Occasional mis-hears: "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cash" in a few places.
